newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan reprimanded for Sumitomo loans.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan reprimanded for Sumitomo loans.

text.p: U.S. banking regulators last year dealt J.P. Morgan & Co Inc a mild reprimand for its role in the financing of activities of maverick Japanese copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, a source familiar with the situation said Thursday.
A reprimand via memorandum of understanding ranks among the lowest of disciplinary actions that the Federal Reserve may take.
A spokesman for the Federal Reserve Bank of New York declined comment. Such memorandums as a matter of policy are not publicly disclosed.

"As a regulated company we naturally have a constant dialogue with regulators around the world on dozens of issues at any given time and this dialogue is always private," said a J.P. Morgan spokesman, declining comment on whether the bank has signed such a memoraundum.
Hamanaka, formerly chief copper dealer at Sumitomo Corp, has pleaded guilty to fraud in Japan following the disclosure last year of huge losses from his trading which eventually grew to $2.6 billion.

According to published reports, the Federal Reserve looked at loans made by J.P. Morgan and other U.S. banks which were in the form of derivatives transactions. According to the Wall Street Journal, J.P. Morgan lent $400 million.
No other U.S. banks were reprimanded in connection with the Sumitomo matter, the Journal said.
Although J.P. Morgan has made certain changes in its base metals business since the Sumitomo affair, the spokesman said the decisions related to a change in business strategy.

He said Morgan was now concentrating on value-added products in base metals, such as commodity-linked financing and hedging, but was no longer making markets and providing quotes. He added that J.P. Morgan was still involved in all areas of the precious metals business.

According to J.P. Morgan's annual report for 1996, commodities revenue for the year totaled $34 million out of a total $6.8 billion in revenue. Base metals were believed to be only a fraction of the commodities activty.
A spokesman for Sumitomo in New York said it would be inappropriate for the company to comment.
